newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to extend probe into French textiles aid plan.
newsitem.headline: EU to extend probe into French textiles aid plan.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to extend a probe on Wednesday into a controversial French government plan to help its textile industry, Commission sources said on Tuesday.

The Commission started proceedings in May into a 2.1-billion-franc proposal to reduce salary-linked social security contributions paid by textile, clothing and leather industries in France in order to stimulate job creation.
While encouraging measures to boost employment, the Commission warned at the time that the French plan could distort competition in the European Union.
It was particularly referring to aid granted to companies with more than 50 employees which, in principle, do not benefit from the so-called 'de minimis' rule for state aid.
Under the rule, a company can receive up to 100,000 European currency units in subsidies over a three-year period without seeking EU clearance.

France reacted to the Commission's arguments, saying the plan was necessary to compensate for collective agreements in the sectors concerned which resulted in a reduction in working hours without equivalent pay cuts, the sources said.

"Is it the role of the state to compensate for companies' increased costs due to collective agreements?" a Commission official asked, leaving little doubt that the EU executive did not think that was the case.

The Commission has consistently rejected other recent national attempts to help specific industries resist international competition. It particularly outlawed similar measures for the Italian shoe industry and Belgian export-led firms.
It has encouraged instead a general, across-the-board reduction of contributions to social security schemes as a way to reduce the EU's huge unemployment.
